notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 timestamped Send Interaction With Regions and timestamped Receive Interaction surfaces to the official C++ declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. The Catch2 scenarios cover committed region overlap, a disjoint-region no-fanout designator, lower-bound validation, constrained-recipient queueing before the grant, sent-region callback propagation, timestamp/order/retraction fields, pending-fanout suppression, and a legal Request Retraction callback for an already-delivered nonconstrained overlap-qualified recipient. A dedicated Flush Queue companion exercises the same public send/receive surfaces and proves the conveyed source-region set is preserved before FQG. Separate explicit-source companions exercise ordinary TAR/NMR and the inclusive TARA/NMRA boundaries and preserve the source RegionHandle before each grant. A further explicit-source companion proves the same public surfaces retain that source RegionHandle and deliver exactly once after a Time Constrained disable/re-enable cycle. A focused save/restore companion preserves the queued regional payload, source RegionHandle set, and live retraction designator across an untimed snapshot and proves Flush Queue delivery plus Request Retraction after restore; RL-136 records the Lab cross-service modeling gap. A mixed-member companion delivers the same regional TSO payload under FQR, TARA, and NMRA requests and checks each callback frontier independently. A committed region move also suppresses a previously overlap-qualified queued callback without manufacturing Request Retraction. The accepted filesystem service-report case now has a paired HLA_IMMEDIATE public MOM matrix that decodes the SendInteractionWithRegions service report before the constrained callback, including its Table 5 supplied/returned forms and callback metadata. The failure companion now exercises the same official send surface for invalid interaction, parameter, region, and logical-time inputs and proves the public exception path emits no application callback while the service-report routes are checked separately. The shared recipient planner ignores passive regional pairs and routes only active overlap-qualified pairs; the current timestamped cases do not independently exercise a passive pair. Object-region services, relaxed DDM, further alternate advance forms, timed/durable restore, remote transport, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
